house.kind: Deck reconstruction of the TPS house
house.reference: slides/tps-and-ai/slides.md: Two houses, different layers; claim 2

jit.reference: slides/tps-and-ai/slides.md: Just-in-Time, from line 990; claims 3, 4 and 17
jit.boundary: Synchronized flow with minimum ready stocks; not zero inventory or everything made from scratch after an order.

resourceful.kind: Terry's interpretation, inspired by Kazumasa Ebata's oral teaching
resourceful.reference: slides/tps-and-ai/slides.md: JIT entrusts people; claims 3, 4 and 14
resourceful.boundary: Neither a Toyota definition nor an authenticated Toyota/Ohno quotation. Scarcity alone does not create capability.

pull.reference: slides/tps-and-ai/slides.md: Pull: smaller customer problems and feedback; claim 17
pull.boundary: A small useful customer outcome pulls necessary work; standards and owned checks still apply.

integration.kind: Continuous-integration practice and Terry's collaboration synthesis
integration.reference: slides/tps-and-ai/slides.md: Integration and coordination; claims 8 and 21
integration.boundary: Frequent small mainline changes keep a working product; an automated green build alone is insufficient.

scenes.label: JIT: Ready to Respond
scenes.heading: JIT

captionRanges.spoken: AI can produce more. But can your team respond better?
A stockpile of generated code is still a stockpile.

scenes.action: Fully composed title and complete stockpile painting at frame zero. Preserve the green signal, full tower and person.

scenes.label: Toyota Production System
scenes.heading: Toyota Production System

captionRanges.spoken: Just-in-Time is the other pillar of the Toyota Production System.
Only what is needed, when needed, in the amount needed.
Minimum stock. Dependable flow. Not constant activity.

scenes.action: Reuse the shared TPS house, highlighting its JIT pillar. The Jidoka edition's default highlight remains unchanged.

scenes.label: Capable response
scenes.heading: Capable response.

captionRanges.spoken: JIT entrusts capable people to respond to real need.
Be resourceful with what you have.

scenes.action: Show the whole original doorway, loaded cart, people and checked ramp. This is a resourcefulness analogy, not a Toyota plant.

scenes.label: One useful outcome
scenes.heading: One useful outcome.

captionRanges.spoken: Pull a small customer problem, not a queue of technical tasks.
Let one useful, end-to-end outcome pull the necessary work.
Use AI for what this need requires.

scenes.action: Fit the complete customer-need illustration. Let the highlighted train remain the first useful smaller outcome.

scenes.label: Choose again
scenes.heading: Choose again.

captionRanges.spoken: Check known quality in the shared, working product.
Use feedback to choose again. Leave later work unstarted.

scenes.action: Fit the complete feedback illustration. Feedback guides the next choice while later work remains unstarted.

scenes.label: Integration pulls collaboration
scenes.heading:
Integrate continuously.
Collaborate just in time.

captionRanges.spoken: Integrate small changes continuously. Keep one coherent product.
When a dependency becomes real, let it pull collaboration.
Technical excellence makes that response dependable.

scenes.action: Successive focused original-art views preserve actual need → teams → stop → collaboration → coherent result. Keep faces, hands and product legible; no crowded status labels or tiny panorama.

scenes.label: Ready to respond
scenes.heading: Ready to respond.

captionRanges.spoken: Build capability to respond, not stockpiles of generated answers.

scenes.action: Hold the collaboration and complete coherent result with all faces and product. Exact Terry credit replaces captions for the final three seconds as the approved score fades.
